items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Row, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Tony Williams influenced a lot of drummers: Buddy Rich used to say when Tony came on, “Oh yeah, great drummer, flounder, flounder. Lightweight. Flounder.”

ctx.x: I remember reading a quote from Lester Young, like no bombs just tickety-tickety or something like that.

Yeah. Titty-boom baby, Titty boom. You know? That’s what happened when the drummers, Elvin was there, I was there in 1963 when they recorded “Live at Birdland.” And Elvin influenced a lot of drummers, and then Tony Williams influenced a lot of drummers: Buddy Rich used to say when Tony came on, “Oh yeah, great drummer, flounder, flounder. Lightweight. Flounder.”

items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I went John Coltrane fast first, because I kept up with Tony Williams, I came up in that era.

ctx.x: Well you know we usually wrap up the interviews by asking do you have any words of wisdom for up and coming musicians, but you just did an hour of it.

Well the whole thing I can say is stick to the basics of things, and keep it simple. It doesn’t have to be complicated. The more complicated it gets, the worse — you’ll never see the pattern of what’s really going on, musically. Listen to a lot of things like the Three Sounds, the old Three Sounds records, and listen to them do it slowly. Then you hear it all. Look at the paper, look at the ups, look at the downs, then you will hear the simple form of things, how it’s supposed to go. Everything is moving too…

Well it’s been — I wish you lived in the States —but I’m glad you’re happy where you are — and get to hear you more. But I’m glad we had this opportunity and I hope that we’ll get to hear you play again, of course tonight we will, but some time in the future.
